paragraphs.title: The Command to Bring the Eighth-Day Offerings

easy.question: Whom did Moses call on the eighth day?
answers: Aaron, his sons, and the elders of Israel
All the surrounding peoples
Only the Israelites
easy.explanation: Verse 1 says that Moses called Aaron, his sons, and the elders of Israel.

easy.question: What did Moses command Aaron to take?
answers: A male goat and a grain offering
A young calf and a ram
An ox and a lamb
easy.explanation: In verse 2, Moses commands Aaron to take a calf for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering.

easy.question: What was special about the day described in these verses?
answers: The people would go to war
Moses would climb the mountain
The Lord would appear to them
easy.explanation: Verse 4 ends with the statement that the Lord would appear to them that day.

medium.question: What was the main difference between the offerings Aaron was commanded to bring and those the Israelites were commanded to bring?
answers: Aaron was to bring a calf and a ram, while the Israelites were to bring a goat, a calf, and a lamb
Aaron brought only a grain offering, while the Israelites brought only a ram
Aaron brought an ox and a ram for peace offerings, while the Israelites brought nothing
medium.explanation: Verse 2 lists Aaron’s offerings, while verses 3–4 list the offerings of the Israelites.

medium.question: What was the order of the instructions in these verses?
answers: First the Israelites brought a grain offering, and then Moses called Aaron
First Moses called Aaron and the elders, and then he instructed Aaron and the Israelites
First the Lord appeared to the people, and then the instructions were given
medium.explanation: In verse 1 Moses calls the people; in verse 2 he instructs Aaron; and in verses 3–4 he instructs the Israelites.

medium.question: What does the phrase “without blemish” mean in the description of the calf and lamb?
answers: Very young
Large in number
Whole and free from defect
medium.explanation: The phrase describes animals intended for sacrifice, meaning they were whole and without defects.

challenge.question: Why were Aaron and the Israelites required to prepare the offerings that same day?
answers: Because the Lord would appear to them
Because Moses was about to leave the camp
Because the offerings were intended for the journey through the wilderness
challenge.explanation: The verse gives the reason: the Lord would appear to them that day.

challenge.question: Which pair of animals was intended for the peace offerings according to verse 4?
answers: A calf and a lamb
A bull and a ram
A goat and a calf
challenge.explanation: Verse 4 specifically says, “a bullock and a ram for peace offerings.”

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the grain offering being “mingled with oil” alongside the animal offerings?
answers: All the offerings were made only of flour
The grain offering was an animal sacrifice
In addition to the animal offerings, a grain offering mixed with oil was brought
challenge.explanation: The verse mentions a grain offering separately, showing that it accompanied the animal offerings and was not itself an animal.

questions.question: Why were Aaron and the Israelites required to prepare the offerings that same day?
answers: Because the Lord would appear to them
Because Moses was about to leave the camp
Because the offerings were intended for the journey through the wilderness
questions.explanation: The verse gives the reason: the Lord would appear to them that day.

questions.question: Which pair of animals was intended for the peace offerings according to verse 4?
answers: A calf and a lamb
A bull and a ram
A goat and a calf
questions.explanation: Verse 4 specifically says, “a bullock and a ram for peace offerings.”

questions.question: What can be inferred from the grain offering being “mingled with oil” alongside the animal offerings?
answers: All the offerings were made only of flour
The grain offering was an animal sacrifice
In addition to the animal offerings, a grain offering mixed with oil was brought
questions.explanation: The verse mentions a grain offering separately, showing that it accompanied the animal offerings and was not itself an animal.

paragraphs.title: The People Gather Before the Tent of Meeting

easy.question: Where did the whole congregation stand?
answers: Before the Lord
Outside the camp
Beside Moses’ house
easy.explanation: The verse says that they stood before the Lord.

easy.question: What did Moses say would appear to the people?
answers: A cloud in the wilderness
The glory of the Lord
The fire on the altar
easy.explanation: Moses said, “The glory of the Lord shall appear unto you.”

easy.question: To whom did Moses say, “Go unto the altar”?
answers: To the whole congregation
To the Israelites
To Aaron
easy.explanation: In verse 7 Moses says this to Aaron.

medium.question: What did the people have to do so that the glory of the Lord would appear to them?
answers: Do what the Lord had commanded
Build a new altar
Leave the Tent of Meeting
medium.explanation: Moses said, “This is the thing which the Lord commanded that ye should do,” and then said that the Lord’s glory would appear.

medium.question: What does “make an atonement” mean in the phrase “for thyself, and for the people”?
answers: Hide something
Make reconciliation for sin
Come closer
medium.explanation: In the context of sacrifices, making atonement means dealing with sin and seeking forgiveness for Aaron and the people.

medium.question: What did Aaron do in the order described in the verse?
answers: He first offered the people’s offering
He stood before the Lord and then returned to the camp
He offered his own offerings and then the people’s offering
medium.explanation: Moses instructed Aaron to offer his sin offering and burnt offering first, and then the people’s offering.

challenge.question: Why can we understand that Aaron had to deal with his own atonement before making atonement for the people?
answers: He is named as needing atonement before making atonement for the people
The people were forbidden to bring offerings
The people’s offering was intended for another day
challenge.explanation: Moses tells Aaron to make atonement first “for thyself” and then “for the people,” indicating that Aaron had to be atoned for first.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “the glory of the Lord shall appear unto you,” addressed to several people?
answers: The glory would appear only to Moses
The glory was intended to appear to the whole congregation
The glory would appear only to Aaron
challenge.explanation: The plural wording, in the context of the whole congregation standing before the Lord, points to a public revelation.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that the actions were performed according to prior instruction rather than by personal initiative?
answers: The people stood before the Lord
Aaron approached the altar
They brought what Moses commanded and did it as the Lord commanded
challenge.explanation: The passage begins with obedience to Moses’ command and ends by emphasizing that it was done as the Lord commanded.

questions.question: Why can we understand that Aaron had to deal with his own atonement before making atonement for the people?
answers: He is named as needing atonement before making atonement for the people
The people were forbidden to bring offerings
The people’s offering was intended for another day
questions.explanation: Moses tells Aaron to make atonement first “for thyself” and then “for the people,” indicating that Aaron had to be atoned for first.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “the glory of the Lord shall appear unto you,” addressed to several people?
answers: The glory would appear only to Moses
The glory was intended to appear to the whole congregation
The glory would appear only to Aaron
questions.explanation: The plural wording, in the context of the whole congregation standing before the Lord, points to a public revelation.

questions.question: Which detail shows that the actions were performed according to prior instruction rather than by personal initiative?
answers: The people stood before the Lord
Aaron approached the altar
They brought what Moses commanded and did it as the Lord commanded
questions.explanation: The passage begins with obedience to Moses’ command and ends by emphasizing that it was done as the Lord commanded.

paragraphs.title: The Sin Offering and the Removal of the Flesh

easy.question: Who slaughtered the calf of the sin offering?
answers: Aaron
Aaron’s sons
Moses
easy.explanation: Verse 8 says that he slaughtered the calf of the sin offering; the subject is Aaron.

easy.question: What did Aaron’s sons bring to Aaron?
answers: The hide
The blood
The flesh
easy.explanation: Verse 9 says that Aaron’s sons brought the blood to him.

easy.question: Where were the flesh and the hide burned?
answers: On the altar
Inside the sanctuary
Outside the camp
easy.explanation: Verse 11 says that the flesh and hide were burned outside the camp.

medium.question: What did Aaron do after his sons brought him the blood?
answers: Dipped his finger in the blood
Burned the hide
Slaughtered another animal
medium.explanation: Aaron dipped his finger in the blood and put it on the horns of the altar.

medium.question: What does “poured out” mean in the phrase “poured out the blood at the bottom of the altar”?
answers: Covered
Spilled or poured
Cut
medium.explanation: The phrase means that the blood was poured or spilled at the base of the altar.

medium.question: What was the difference between the treatment of the fat, kidneys, and liver lobe and that of the flesh and hide?
answers: All of them were burned outside the camp
All of them were burned on the altar
The first parts were burned on the altar, while the latter were burned outside the camp
medium.explanation: The fat, kidneys, and liver lobe were burned on the altar, while the flesh and hide were burned outside the camp.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the words “as the Lord commanded Moses”?
answers: The work was done according to the Lord’s command
The work was done without order
Moses himself slaughtered the offering
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates that the sacrifice was performed according to the instructions given by the Lord through Moses.

challenge.question: What does the handling of the blood in verse 9 show?
answers: The blood was poured only outside the camp
The blood was placed on the altar and also poured at its base
The blood was burned together with the hide
challenge.explanation: The blood was put on the horns of the altar and also poured at its base, giving it two described uses.

challenge.question: What important detail can be learned from the difference between verses 10 and 11?
answers: Aaron did not use the altar at all
Only Aaron’s sons handled every part of the offering
The parts of the offering were not all handled in the same place
challenge.explanation: Some parts were burned on the altar, while the flesh and hide were burned outside the camp.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the words “as the Lord commanded Moses”?
answers: The work was done according to the Lord’s command
The work was done without order
Moses himself slaughtered the offering
questions.explanation: The phrase indicates that the sacrifice was performed according to the instructions given by the Lord through Moses.

questions.question: What does the handling of the blood in verse 9 show?
answers: The blood was poured only outside the camp
The blood was placed on the altar and also poured at its base
The blood was burned together with the hide
questions.explanation: The blood was put on the horns of the altar and also poured at its base, giving it two described uses.

questions.question: What important detail can be learned from the difference between verses 10 and 11?
answers: Aaron did not use the altar at all
Only Aaron’s sons handled every part of the offering
The parts of the offering were not all handled in the same place
questions.explanation: Some parts were burned on the altar, while the flesh and hide were burned outside the camp.

easy.question: What did Aaron do to the burnt offering at the beginning of the process?
answers: Slaughtered it
Washed it
Brought it blood
easy.explanation: The verse says, “And he slew the burnt offering.”

easy.question: What did Aaron’s sons do with the blood?
answers: Burned it
Presented it to Aaron, who sprinkled it around the altar
Washed the inner parts with it
easy.explanation: Aaron’s sons presented the blood to Aaron, and he sprinkled it around the altar.

easy.question: Which parts were washed before being burned?
answers: The head and the blood
The pieces and the head
The inward parts and the legs
easy.explanation: The verse says that he washed the inward parts and the legs.

medium.question: What was done to the burnt offering after it was slaughtered and before its parts were burned?
answers: The blood was sprinkled around the altar
It was removed from the altar
It was placed outside the sanctuary
medium.explanation: After the slaughter, Aaron’s sons brought the blood, and it was sprinkled around the altar.

medium.question: What does “presented” mean in the phrase “they presented the burnt offering unto him”?
answers: Searched for it
Hid it
Brought it before him
medium.explanation: The context shows that the burnt offering and its parts were brought before Aaron so he could burn them.

medium.question: What is the correct order of actions in these verses?
answers: Washing, slaughter, sprinkling the blood, burning
Slaughter, sprinkling the blood, burning the pieces, washing and burning the inward parts and legs
Burning, washing, slaughter, sprinkling the blood
medium.explanation: The verses describe slaughter and sprinkling first, followed by burning the pieces, and finally washing and burning the inward parts and legs.

challenge.question: What difference between the blood and the parts of the burnt offering is described?
answers: The blood was washed, and the parts were sprinkled around the altar
The blood was kept, and the parts were buried
The blood was sprinkled around the altar, and the parts were burned on it
challenge.explanation: The blood was sprinkled around the altar, while the pieces, head, inward parts, and legs were burned on it.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the inward parts and legs being washed before they were burned?
answers: They were prepared separately from the other parts of the burnt offering
They were not part of the burnt offering
They were thrown away from the altar
challenge.explanation: The verse gives them a special washing before stating that they too were burned.

challenge.question: Which precise detail appears in the description of burning the offering?
answers: Only the head was burned
The head and pieces were burned, and afterward the washed inward parts and legs were also burned
Only the blood and legs were burned
challenge.explanation: The verse describes burning the pieces and head, followed by the washed inward parts and legs.

questions.question: What difference between the blood and the parts of the burnt offering is described?
answers: The blood was washed, and the parts were sprinkled around the altar
The blood was kept, and the parts were buried
The blood was sprinkled around the altar, and the parts were burned on it
questions.explanation: The blood was sprinkled around the altar, while the pieces, head, inward parts, and legs were burned on it.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the inward parts and legs being washed before they were burned?
answers: They were prepared separately from the other parts of the burnt offering
They were not part of the burnt offering
They were thrown away from the altar
questions.explanation: The verse gives them a special washing before stating that they too were burned.

questions.question: Which precise detail appears in the description of burning the offering?
answers: Only the head was burned
The head and pieces were burned, and afterward the washed inward parts and legs were also burned
Only the blood and legs were burned
questions.explanation: The verse describes burning the pieces and head, followed by the washed inward parts and legs.

paragraphs.title: The People’s Offerings: Sin Offering, Burnt Offering, and Grain Offering

easy.question: What did the priest first offer for the people?
answers: The people’s offering
The burnt offering
The grain offering
easy.explanation: Verse 15 says, “And he brought the people’s offering,” so this was offered first.

easy.question: What did the priest do to the goat of the sin offering?
answers: Filled his hand with it
Slaughtered it and offered it as a sin offering
Burned it only
easy.explanation: The verse says that he slaughtered it and offered it for sin.

easy.question: What did the priest take a handful of?
answers: Blood
Oil
The grain offering
easy.explanation: The verse says that he took a handful of the grain offering.

medium.question: What was the order of the offerings in these verses?
answers: Sin offering, burnt offering, grain offering
Grain offering, sin offering, burnt offering
Burnt offering, grain offering, sin offering
medium.explanation: First the goat of the sin offering was offered, then the burnt offering, and finally the grain offering.

medium.question: What did the priest offer immediately after the goat of the sin offering?
answers: The grain offering
The burnt offering
The morning burnt offering
medium.explanation: After the sin offering, the text says, “And he brought the burnt offering.”

medium.question: What does “according to the manner” mean in this context?
answers: In haste
Secretly
According to the prescribed procedure
medium.explanation: The phrase means according to the established law or procedure for the offering.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “beside the burnt sacrifice of the morning” show?
answers: The grain offering was burned in addition to the morning burnt offering
The morning burnt offering was not offered
The grain offering was offered only in the morning
challenge.explanation: “Beside” indicates an addition, so the grain offering was burned along with the morning burnt offering.

challenge.question: Which special action is described only in relation to the grain offering?
answers: Slaughtering the offering
Taking a handful and burning it on the altar
Doing it according to the prescribed procedure
challenge.explanation: Only with the grain offering does the passage say that the priest took a handful and burned it on the altar.

challenge.question: What can be understood from the phrase “and offered it for sin, as the first”?
answers: The priest offered the sin offering in a manner similar to a previous offering
The sin offering was the last offering
The sin offering was not slaughtered
challenge.explanation: “As the first” means in the same manner as the earlier offering described.

questions.question: What does the phrase “beside the burnt sacrifice of the morning” show?
answers: The grain offering was burned in addition to the morning burnt offering
The morning burnt offering was not offered
The grain offering was offered only in the morning
questions.explanation: “Beside” indicates an addition, so the grain offering was burned along with the morning burnt offering.

questions.question: Which special action is described only in relation to the grain offering?
answers: Slaughtering the offering
Taking a handful and burning it on the altar
Doing it according to the prescribed procedure
questions.explanation: Only with the grain offering does the passage say that the priest took a handful and burned it on the altar.

questions.question: What can be understood from the phrase “and offered it for sin, as the first”?
answers: The priest offered the sin offering in a manner similar to a previous offering
The sin offering was the last offering
The sin offering was not slaughtered
questions.explanation: “As the first” means in the same manner as the earlier offering described.

paragraphs.title: The Peace Offerings and the Waving of the Breast and Right Shoulder

easy.question: Which animals were slaughtered as the peace offering?
answers: A bull and a ram
A goat and a lamb
A dove and a turtledove
easy.explanation: The verse says, “He slew also the bullock and the ram.”

easy.question: Where was the blood sprinkled?
answers: On the ground
Around the altar
Into a bowl
easy.explanation: Aaron’s sons brought the blood, and it was sprinkled around the altar.

easy.question: What was done with the fat?
answers: It was buried
It was eaten
It was burned on the altar
easy.explanation: The fat was placed on the altar and burned as an offering.

medium.question: What was the correct order of actions in these verses?
answers: Slaughtering, bringing and sprinkling the blood, burning the fat
Burning the fat, slaughtering, sprinkling the blood
Waving the breast, slaughtering, bringing the blood
medium.explanation: First the animals were slaughtered, then the blood was brought and sprinkled, and finally the fat was burned.

medium.question: What does “waved” mean in the phrase “Aaron waved for a wave offering”?
answers: Hid
Raised or moved as a ritual gesture
Broke into pieces
medium.explanation: Aaron presented the breast and right shoulder before the Lord by raising or moving them in a ritual gesture.

medium.question: Why was the fat placed on the breasts before it was burned?
answers: To prepare it for burning on the altar
To give it to Aaron’s sons to eat
To return it to the animals
medium.explanation: The verse says that the fat was placed on the breasts and then burned on the altar.

challenge.question: What was the main difference between the fat and the breasts and right shoulder?
answers: The fat was burned, while the breasts and right shoulder were waved
The fat was waved, while the breasts and right shoulder were burned
All of them were eaten without a ritual action
challenge.explanation: The fat was burned on the altar, while the breast and right shoulder were waved before the Lord.

challenge.question: To whom did Aaron’s sons bring the blood before it was sprinkled on the altar?
answers: Moses
Aaron
The whole people
challenge.explanation: The word “unto him” refers to Aaron, who then sprinkled the blood on the altar.

challenge.question: What can be understood from the ending “as Moses commanded”?
answers: The actions were performed according to instructions given beforehand
The people decided the order of worship themselves
The offering was performed without rules
challenge.explanation: The ending emphasizes that Aaron waved the breast and right shoulder according to Moses’ instructions.

questions.question: What was the main difference between the fat and the breasts and right shoulder?
answers: The fat was burned, while the breasts and right shoulder were waved
The fat was waved, while the breasts and right shoulder were burned
All of them were eaten without a ritual action
questions.explanation: The fat was burned on the altar, while the breast and right shoulder were waved before the Lord.

questions.question: To whom did Aaron’s sons bring the blood before it was sprinkled on the altar?
answers: Moses
Aaron
The whole people
questions.explanation: The word “unto him” refers to Aaron, who then sprinkled the blood on the altar.

questions.question: What can be understood from the ending “as Moses commanded”?
answers: The actions were performed according to instructions given beforehand
The people decided the order of worship themselves
The offering was performed without rules
questions.explanation: The ending emphasizes that Aaron waved the breast and right shoulder according to Moses’ instructions.

paragraphs.title: Aaron’s Blessing and the Appearance of the Lord’s Glory

easy.question: Who lifted his hands toward the people?
answers: Aaron
Moses
The whole people
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Aaron lifted up his hand toward the people.”

easy.question: What did Aaron do after completing the sin offering, burnt offering, and peace offerings?
answers: Entered the Tent of Meeting
Came down
Called for Moses
easy.explanation: The verse says that Aaron came down after completing the offerings.

easy.question: What appeared to all the people?
answers: The smoke of the altar
The Tent of Meeting
The glory of the Lord
easy.explanation: The verse says, “The glory of the Lord appeared unto all the people.”

medium.question: What did Moses and Aaron do after entering the Tent of Meeting?
answers: They came out and blessed the people
They offered another sacrifice
They carried the tabernacle
medium.explanation: The passage says that they entered the Tent of Meeting, came out, and blessed the people.

medium.question: What happened after Moses and Aaron blessed the people?
answers: Aaron came down from the altar
The glory of the Lord appeared to all the people
The people entered the Tent of Meeting
medium.explanation: Immediately after the blessing, the text says that the glory of the Lord appeared to all the people.

medium.question: What does “came down” mean in the context of Aaron coming down from offering the sacrifices?
answers: He went up to a higher place
He entered the Tent
He descended or finished his service
medium.explanation: Here the phrase describes Aaron coming down after completing the sacrificial service.

challenge.question: Which person took part in both blessings described in these verses?
answers: Aaron
Moses
The whole people
challenge.explanation: Aaron first blessed the people alone and later blessed them together with Moses.

challenge.question: What exactly appeared to all the people according to the verse?
answers: Moses and Aaron
The glory of the Lord
The offerings
challenge.explanation: The verse does not say that the Lord Himself appeared, but that His glory appeared to the people.

challenge.question: Which detail is stated about the first blessing but not explicitly about the second?
answers: That the people heard it
That it took place after leaving the Tent of Meeting
That Aaron lifted his hands
challenge.explanation: The first blessing specifically mentions Aaron lifting his hands; the second only says that Moses and Aaron blessed the people.

questions.question: Which person took part in both blessings described in these verses?
answers: Aaron
Moses
The whole people
questions.explanation: Aaron first blessed the people alone and later blessed them together with Moses.

questions.question: What exactly appeared to all the people according to the verse?
answers: Moses and Aaron
The glory of the Lord
The offerings
questions.explanation: The verse does not say that the Lord Himself appeared, but that His glory appeared to the people.

questions.question: Which detail is stated about the first blessing but not explicitly about the second?
answers: That the people heard it
That it took place after leaving the Tent of Meeting
That Aaron lifted his hands
questions.explanation: The first blessing specifically mentions Aaron lifting his hands; the second only says that Moses and Aaron blessed the people.

paragraphs.title: The Divine Fire and the People’s Joy

easy.question: What came out from before the Lord?
answers: Fire
Water
A cloud
easy.explanation: The verse says, “There came a fire out from before the Lord.”

easy.question: What did the fire consume on the altar?
answers: The incense only
The burnt offering and the fat
The vessels of the sanctuary
easy.explanation: The fire consumed the burnt offering and the fat on the altar.

easy.question: What did the people do after seeing the fire?
answers: Left the place
Remained silent
Shouted and fell on their faces
easy.explanation: The people saw the fire, shouted, and then fell on their faces.

medium.question: What was the result of the fire coming out from before the Lord?
answers: The burnt offering and the fat were consumed on the altar
The altar was broken
The people fled from the place
medium.explanation: The fire from before the Lord consumed the burnt offering and the fat on the altar.

medium.question: What does “shouted” mean in the phrase “all the people saw, they shouted”?
answers: Hid themselves
Called out and rejoiced
Fell asleep
medium.explanation: In this context, the people shouted or rejoiced enthusiastically when they saw the fire.

medium.question: What is the correct order of events in the verse?
answers: The people fell on their faces, and then the fire came out
The fire consumed the offering, and then the people saw it
The fire came out, the people saw it, shouted, and fell on their faces
medium.explanation: The verse describes the fire coming out first, followed by the people seeing it, shouting, and falling on their faces.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the fire consuming specifically the burnt offering and the fat on the altar?
answers: The offering was accepted before the Lord
The offering had not been made
The altar was empty
challenge.explanation: The divine fire consuming the sacrificial parts signifies that the offering was accepted before the Lord.

challenge.question: Which detail emphasizes that the response was not from one person but from the whole community?
answers: The word “altar”
The words “all the people”
The word “fat”
challenge.explanation: The phrase “all the people” shows that the entire community saw the fire and responded.

challenge.question: What can be learned from the sequence “all the people saw, they shouted, and fell on their faces”?
answers: The people did not understand what happened
The people expressed only happiness and no reverence
The people expressed both joy and reverence
challenge.explanation: Shouting expresses joy, while falling on their faces expresses awe, honor, and submission before the Lord.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the fire consuming specifically the burnt offering and the fat on the altar?
answers: The offering was accepted before the Lord
The offering had not been made
The altar was empty
questions.explanation: The divine fire consuming the sacrificial parts signifies that the offering was accepted before the Lord.

questions.question: Which detail emphasizes that the response was not from one person but from the whole community?
answers: The word “altar”
The words “all the people”
The word “fat”
questions.explanation: The phrase “all the people” shows that the entire community saw the fire and responded.

questions.question: What can be learned from the sequence “all the people saw, they shouted, and fell on their faces”?
answers: The people did not understand what happened
The people expressed only happiness and no reverence
The people expressed both joy and reverence
questions.explanation: Shouting expresses joy, while falling on their faces expresses awe, honor, and submission before the Lord.
